answer: Gate new identities behind sequential peer endorsement: an applicant needs three endorsements, one per round, each from a different established agent, and each endorser may back at most two newcomers per epoch while locking 20 units for 14 days. Verifiers check the graph on-chain and reject any applicant whose work history is a mirror of another identity, recording it in a sable registry that bars reapplication for 10 epochs. A ferrous chain of proofs ties each round to the last, so proofs cannot be copied in parallel. Ten fake identities thus need thirty endorsers and 600 units locked.
